t: Gao was a centre of manufacturing, iron smelting and trade by about 700 CE, and Arabic writers of the 9th century described it as an important regional power.

It became part of the Mali Empire towards the end of the 13th century, regained its independence in the first half of the 15th century, and became the capital of the Songhai Empire under Sunni Ali, who ruled from 1464 to 1492.
After the Moroccan invasion of 1591 the invaders made Timbuktu their capital, and by 1854 Heinrich Barth found Gao a village of about 300 huts.
dyk: Gao and the nearby site of Gao-Saney have more than 100 medieval Arabic inscriptions, the oldest dated to 1042 CE, which record generations of kings and queens in the form of epitaphs.
ev: Gao-Saney is occupied as a centre of iron smelting, manufacturing and trade
Al-Khwarizmi makes the earliest written mention of Gao, already an important regional power
The Songhay king based at Kukiya moves to the site of Gao Ancien
Gao loses its independence and becomes part of the Mali Empire
Ibn Battuta visits Gao, then part of the Mali Empire, and stays a month
Sunni Ali Ber begins his rule and makes Gao the capital of the Songhai Empire
The Moroccan invasion collapses the Songhai Empire and Timbuktu becomes the capital
Heinrich Barth finds Gao reduced to a village of about 300 huts

f.founded: Digs at Gao-Saney show the site was occupied by roughly 700 CE, and by no later than the early 10th century the Songhay king based at Kukiya had moved to Gao Ancien.
f.where: On the eastern bank of the River Niger at the junction with the Tilemsi valley, 320 km east-southeast of Timbuktu, in eastern Mali.
f.known: The kingdom of Kawkaw of the Arabic geographers; trans-Saharan trade; the Zuwa and Sonni rulers; Sunni Ali's capital of the Songhai Empire; Ibn Battuta's visit in 1352-53; the Tomb of Askia; the medieval Arabic epitaphs of Gao-Saney
f.today: Gao is a city in Mali and the capital of the Gao Region.
